subject: Agriculture
title: Loss of Crop Diversity
description: A quick win: understand Loss of Crop Diversity.

hook.text: India once grew 30,000 rice varieties. Today, a handful dominate. The rest are nearly extinct.

buildup.text: Green Revolution varieties replaced thousands of local landraces that had adapted over centuries.

discovery.text: Each lost variety carried unique genes—drought tolerance, pest resistance, flavor—evolved over millennia.

twist.text: If a new disease strikes modern varieties, the genes to fight it may already be extinct.

climax.text: Seed banks like Svalbard store samples, but frozen seeds can't evolve. Living diversity is irreplaceable.

punchline.text: We chose the most productive seeds and lost the rest. Efficiency ate diversity.

quiz.question: How many rice varieties did India historically grow before the Green Revolution?

details.summary: The Green Revolution replaced thousands of locally adapted traditional crop varieties with a handful of high-yielding modern cultivars, dramatically reducing agricultural biodiversity. This genetic narrowing makes global food production more vulnerable to new diseases and climate disruption.
details.whyItMatters: Traditional varieties carry genetic traits for drought tolerance, pest resistance, and nutritional quality that have been lost as farmers abandoned them for Green Revolution cultivars.
takeaways: The Green Revolution replaced thousands of traditional rice varieties with just a few lines
75% of global crop genetic diversity has been lost since the early twentieth century
Gene banks now preserve over 7 million crop samples to safeguard future breeding options

faq.question: How did the Green Revolution reduce crop genetic diversity?
faq.answer: High-yielding modern varieties were so productive that farmers abandoned thousands of locally adapted traditional varieties. In India, farmers grew over 30,000 rice varieties in the 1960s; by the 1990s, 75% of rice area was planted with just 10 varieties. Similar genetic narrowing occurred globally.

faq.question: Why does crop genetic diversity matter for food security?
faq.answer: Traditional varieties carry genes for drought tolerance, disease resistance, pest adaptation, and nutritional qualities. When a new disease or climate shift threatens a major crop, breeders need diverse genetic material to develop resistant varieties.
